name: B.Ed
title: B.Ed — Becoming a School Teacher in India
intro: The teaching roadmap: B.Ed or ITEP admission, internship in schools, teacher eligibility tests and government and private teaching jobs.

phases.title: Choose your route
phases.summary: Two-year B.Ed after a bachelor’s degree, or the four-year integrated ITEP after Class 12.
points: B.Ed (2 years): open to graduates, usually with at least 50% marks, in subjects that match school teaching.
ITEP (4 years): integrated teacher education programme after Class 12, admission through the National Common Entrance Test (NCET) conducted by NTA.
Check that the college is recognised by the National Council for Teacher Education (NCTE).
Pick teaching subjects (e.g., Maths, Science, Social Science, English) according to your degree.

phases.title: Entrance exams and admission
phases.summary: State B.Ed CETs, university entrances and NCET.
points: Take your state’s B.Ed entrance (e.g., state CETs) or the university’s own test.
Apply for NCET for ITEP seats in participating institutions.
Counselling allots colleges according to rank.
Submit your degree certificates and complete admission.

phases.title: Course structure
phases.summary: Foundations of education, pedagogy and school subjects.
points: Learn Educational Psychology, Philosophy and Sociology of Education, Curriculum Studies and Assessment.
Study pedagogy of two school subjects and use ICT in teaching.
Take courses on inclusive education, gender and school management.
Learn lesson planning, classroom management and communication.

phases.title: School internship and teaching practice
phases.summary: Several weeks of teaching in real schools under mentor teachers.
points: Complete the school internship period required by NCTE guidelines.
Observe lessons, plan units, teach classes and get feedback from mentors.
Prepare a portfolio with lesson plans, reflections and teaching aids.
Complete practical assessments.

phases.title: Teacher eligibility tests and jobs
phases.summary: CTET and state TETs are needed for most government school jobs.
points: CTET (conducted by CBSE) has Paper I for classes 1–5 and Paper II for classes 6–8; clearing it gives eligibility for central schools like KVS and NVS and many private schools.
State TETs apply to government schools in each state.
Recruitment: KVS, NVS, DSSSB, state teacher recruitment and private schools.
Further study: M.Ed, UGC NET and PhD for higher education.
facts: KVS, NVS, state boards, private schools
